pitch_detail.notes: Starts from a ledge. Clip the first hanger, then work up and a little left, crossing a right-slanting feature. Pleasant moderate rock leads to ledges near the top and the chain anchor.
Leaves the belay going up and right past a few hangers to the next anchor. Easy ground, graded 5th class in the topo notes.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches with lengths, bolt counts and anchors. No rappel table: text only says to walk right to a chain anchor and make two rappels.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble low-angle rock up a shallow gully to the first bolt about 25 ft up. Continue over a slab band into steeper rock with big holds; the angle relaxes before the chain anchor.
About 25 ft up and slightly right gets you to a ledge and the first bolt. Then head straight up easy-angled rock with a few slab moves; the finish is a simple scramble to the top-of-crag anchor.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. No rappel table: only a walk to a chain anchor and two rappels is given.

pitch_detail.notes: A bouldery notch leaves the ground, passing hanging alders. Intermittent cracks then lead up ground that alternates between steep and low angle to a two-bolt belay.
Easy ground with spaced gear up to a lone bolt used as a transition anchor.
Traverse right across a polished slab to reach a blunt arete jutting from the face. Moderate climbing with spaced gear ends at a grassy ledge with a two-bolt belay.
Stay on the moderate arete with spaced protection to the next two-bolt belay.

pitch_detail.anchor: 2-bolt belay under the next steeper wall
pitch_detail.notes: Scrambling up the arete and across a broad grassy ledge to a two-bolt belay below a steeper wall.
Steepish moderate wall of lovely rock, then a runout easy slab ends at the two-bolt anchor on top of the route. Hike up gentle rock to the meadows above, or rappel from here.

review.changed: Wrote all 6 pitches with grades, lengths and anchors. No crux flagged (none named). No rappel table: no stations listed.

pitch_detail.notes: Begins atop the 4th class pitch of the neighbouring route. Instead of traversing left around the tower, climb steep flakes and blocks just left of the tower's sharp arete and belay on a large grassy ledge.

Traverse left along the grassy ledge to a clean hand crack in a snug corner that faces right. Pull a small roof near its top to reach the summit area, then roughly 100 ft of 3rd class scrambling finishes on the true summit.

review.changed: Wrote the two pitches this variation adds (numbered 5 and 6 in the linked-up description); labelled 1 and 2 here. Pitch 2 grade 5.6 comes from the intro sentence about the hand-crack corner.

pitch_detail.notes: Follow the obvious splitter that begins as finger crack and soon widens to hands, zigzagging near the top. From the ledge above, step right about 15 ft and climb a juggy, easy (about 5.6) but poorly protected slab to the ledge below a shallow roof. A 60 m rope reaches that ledge; with a 50 m rope, anchors can be built left or right below the roof.
These two are best linked. Go around the shallow roof system on the far left, then trend back right above the belayer toward a thin, less-than-vertical finger crack.
Climb the thin finger crack in the system above the earlier pitches. It leads to the top, where plenty of boulders can be slung for a belay.

review.changed: Wrote pitch 1, linked pitches 2-3 and pitch 4. Pitch 2-3 has no stated grade. No lengths stated apart from the rope remark.
review.other_findings: Source says the original ascent wandered on pitches 2 and 3 and recommends a more direct line.

pitch_detail.notes: Starting beside the gully, six feet to its right, on dark streaked stone, clip a bolt about 10 ft up and two more hangers. Pull a dirty ledge, then place cams and nuts in the midsection until a final bolt guards a bulge. Big holds trending up and left reach a good belay ledge.

Step right off the chain anchor and go about 10 ft to the first bolt. A bulge gives more technical climbing, and a short steep move past a ledge, protected by the fourth bolt, precedes the two-hanger anchor.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. Pitch grades given only in French style (4b) so omitted; bolt counts per pitch ambiguous so omitted. No rappel table: only a double rappel from anchors to the left is mentioned.

pitch_detail.notes: Starts below an obvious splitter crack coming off the glacier. Follow a right-trending crack system until a thin 15 ft leftward traverse reaches the splitter hand crack, which leads to a ledge below a red rock face.

Traverse right along the ledge under the red face into a 4th class gully for two pitches, then work back left to the foot of the white pillar. A direct link from the top of pitch 1 was wet and dirty on the first ascent, so the detour was used.
Start under the red corner in the middle of the face. Cracks, flakes and face holds lead to a small ledge below the corner.
Stem and jam up the red corner to a ledge below the final left-facing dihedral.
Climb the dihedral with thin stemming low, then a layback handcrack taking a number 0.75 cam, and an easy corner exits the headwall.
A short handcrack on the ridge reaches lower-angle ground.
Ridge terrain, 4th to 5th class, to the base of the last steep pitch below the summit.
Steep twin cracks, a little right of the summit snowfield, lead to 4th class terrain and the top.

review.changed: Wrote the 8 entries covering all 10 pitches (2-3 and 8-9 linked as in the text). No anchors or bolt counts stated. Descent options are not rappel station lists.

pitch_detail.notes: Start in a dihedral tucked behind two parallel saguaros. Good gear in a crack running from fingers to hands, then over a ledge and up a short face past a large loose block (avoidable, or trundle it). Belay in a protected corner with cams from half an inch to three inches.
A short face beside a wide crack. The main ridge can be gained directly, though a slight rightward traverse also works. Belay on a ledge.
Keep following the ridge over a series of ledges and one step across into the last stretch of ridge. Belay on cracks or blocks beside a saguaro.
Take the rope off or simul-climb roughly 200 ft of gentle ridge to reach the true summit.

review.changed: Wrote all four pitches. No lengths, bolts or anchors stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Loose sandstone at the start leads to better rock with little fall risk. A roof about halfway up is pulled onto the next band of rock, one of the harder spots on the route.
Starts from a hanging belay with nowhere to rest or shed gear. The rock is better here, though several stretches rely on small crimps.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches from loose prose; no grades, lengths or bolt counts stated, so none added.

pitch_detail.notes: The easiest pitch, with large holds to a standing belay. The base belay sits on a steep slope, so anchor in there.
Climbs a crack to another standing belay. Raptors nest beside this pitch and the wall is closed to climbers from March through May.
Goes off the right side of the pitch 2 belay up to the last anchor. Belays are roomy and comfortable.

review.changed: Wrote three pitches; no grades, lengths or bolt counts stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Cross the bergschrund and move onto rock about 80 ft (27 m) above it. Easy ice.
Go up ice and snow along the rock of the north ridge to a larger ramp. Belay above the ramp, then down-climb across to it. Easy ice.

Follow the ramp: step around a corner (about 5.3 to 5.4), then several rope lengths leftward with occasional step-across moves of 5.2 to 5.4. Avoid heading up the face on the tempting crack systems. Individual pitch lengths are unknown and probably short.

Class 3 to 4 up the ridge for 150 ft to a step of freshly broken rock. On the second of these, go right onto the face (about 5.4, protected with a 2 in piece) and back to the crest; route-finding is needed, and tackling the step directly is worth considering.
Up the obvious crack in steepening friction to a sheltered belay. Gear from 1 to 2 inches is useful.
Snow and ice. A big piece can serve for a running belay high on pitch 12.
Walk lessening-angle snow to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote 7 entries covering the pitches described (to 14+). Many lengths unknown. No rappel table: descent is discussed generally.
review.other_findings: Stored pitch count 10; text describes 14 or more.

pitch_detail.notes: Cross the moat to rock below the notch between the two crags. Easy, somewhat fractured rock leads to the notch; go through or around it to the west face and traverse left to a comfortable belay under a wide crack or narrow chimney. Rope drag through the notch may argue for splitting it into two pitches.
Climb up to the wide crack, probably the crux (grade uncertain), follow it, then trend up and left to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches; grade 5.6 on pitch 2 is hedged by the text. No lengths stated. No rappel table (descent is by rappelling the west face to the belay ledge, then pitch 1).

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the corner, then partway up shift to the right side of a narrowing chimney-like feature and pass a big chockstone to a belay. Slabby footwork in a few spots.

The chimney keeps narrowing. Printed grades are easy, yet the exit from it is awkward, closer to 5.7 or 5.8 by one climber's feel. Above it, work up and left to a belay at the foot of pitch 3, using nearly a full 60 m rope.
A short, unprotected slab of chicken heads (about 10 m, around 5.4 to 5.5 on the left side) leads to grassy ramps with mostly scrambling and a couple of moves up to about 5.7.
Mostly scrambling or low 5th class over grassy ledges to the foot of the dihedral. Many will link this with the next pitch.

The dihedral corner crack: awkward wide start, narrowing, then widening to fists and wide hands with few face features. The steeper hands-and-fists section is the crux; ledges allow a belay before or after it.
Finish any remaining corner, then grassy ledges to the ridge crest. From there mostly 3rd and 4th class scrambling, with odd low 5th moves, to the summits.

review.changed: Wrote all 6 pitches; grades only where stated firmly. No rappel table (descent gives only rope lengths).

pitch_detail.notes: Start just right of the toe of the rib on easy ramps and belay atop a heather bush.
Carry on upward, then left over the crest of the rib. Some exposed chicken-head face moves drop into a heather gully.

The heather gully offers a few chimney and ledge moves and splits near its top. Choose the right branch to reach the sharp ridge crest (the left branch took a brief aid move on a layback crack). After that, move the belay along the crest until the ridge steepens again.
A brief chimney and some pulls over ledges lead to another vegetated ledge.

The standout pitch. Either squeeze through the cave and a short chimney to a jam crack, or take the 10 m hand crack on the cave's right, which joins in. Hand jams, some wide sections and chicken-head face moves; protects well with mostly hand-size pieces.
A few more chimney moves reach easier ground at the ridge crest. Scramble to the NW summit, then traverse southeast to the main summit.

rappel_detail.notes: From the main summit follow the ridge southeast to the South Summit and rappel skier's left into a blocky alcove.

rappel_detail.anchor: rappel station on the ridge crest
rappel_detail.notes: Traverse out of the alcove on exposed 3rd class following cairns to the crest, then rappel skier's right to grassy ledges. A 60 m rope should just make it, as a rope stretcher.

review.changed: Wrote 6 pitches with lengths and 2 rappels from the summit descent. No grades given per pitch.

pitch_detail.notes: A sustained splitter hand crack beginning at number 2 cam size, narrowing to thin hands and a short finger section at the top, possibly 5.10a there. A couple of rest spots; can be aided if needed.

Climb flakes and ledges leftward, then return rightward. The older guide breaks this into two pitches, but going up and right makes one, especially on a 70 m rope. Easier ground to about 5.7; watch for loose rock.

Head for a dihedral holding twin cracks, then a corner that is stemmed and mantled over. A flaring crack follows (off-width, tightening to fists), awkward for the feet at first. At its top step left across an exposed move to easier ground and belay before the last crack. Mostly mid 5th class, up to about 5.8 or 5.9.
A short wide-hands and fist crack widening to low-angle off-width, though face holds let you avoid the wide climbing. A few 4th or low 5th moves lead to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote four pitches. No rappel table: descent mentions rappels without a clean station list.

pitch_detail.notes: A clean left-leaning tips flake leads into a hand and finger crack (5.9) in a left-facing corner, ending at a good ledge.
From the left end of the ledge, cracks and flakes go straight up to a rightward traverse past loose flakes, to a stance under a large detached block.

Take the corner on the right of the detached block; it faces left and pinches to a seam. A Lost Arrow went in and one French-free move got past it, though awkward stemming could free it. Continue over a bulge to a sloping ledge.
An overhanging handcrack through a bulge, then a clean hand and finger crack (5.10) on the face above, ending on a good ledge.
Move right to a widening left-facing corner, thin hands becoming a squeeze chimney. Belay on top of the big rectangular block.

review.changed: Wrote the 5 variation pitches. Text adds two more pitches of the standard route (5.7) beyond pitch 5, not added. No fixed anchors on route.

pitch_detail.notes: Clean corners and some wet rock, with a fun traverse to the belay. The opening flakes on this line are described as the crux.
Some vegetation, then a long, clean, runout slab traverse to the belay.
Wandering terrain with plenty of edges and very little protection.
About 65 m of glacier-polished rock, thin flakes and low-angle off-width.
Short and simple. A hex placement is available.

review.changed: Wrote five pitches from the brief per-pitch summary; no grades, bolts or anchors stated. Crux not flagged.
